title: PICO_LDR_VP4 Coverage Audit
h1: Does the grouped hunnivirus module work?
standfirst: PICO_LDR_VP4 groups six small genera that share one genome organisation — a leader, the four-capsid-protein layout, a single VPg: Bopivirus, Erbovirus, Mischivirus, Hunnivirus, Tottorivirus and Anativirus. Together they are bovine, equine, bat, duck and rodent viruses that no one would model separately. This is the largest of the four grouped modules and the one where the per-genus picture is most uneven.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Six genera, 201 near-complete exemplars, and two slots holding more than one protein.

blocks.html: Hunnivirus supplies 76 of the routed exemplars, Bopivirus 41, Mischivirus and Anativirus 26 each, Erbovirus 7 and Tottorivirus 6.

rows: genomes in the BV-BRC protein dump

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Fifteen features, 100 profiles, and two genus-conditional splits made before building.

blocks.html: Bopivirus 2A is a 212-residue protein; the other five genera carry 12–55 residue StopGo peptides. Split into 2A (StopGo) and 2A_LONG (Bopivirus).

The Erbovirus leader is a 219-residue protease; the others are 51–84 residues. Split into Ldr and Ldr_PRO. Equine rhinitis B virus L has confirmed C-terminal processing activity (Hinton 2002, J Gen Virol 83:3111, PMID 12466488, model-proposed), so Ldr_PRO takes the existing Leader protease (Lpro) vocabulary string rather than a new one.
Two features in one module must never share an annotation string or a gene symbol; the generator refuses either.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: Windows at 0.8× to 1.2× the collection median; bit cutoffs at 0.45× the median length.

blocks.html: Self-recall against each feature's own in-range collection: 739 of 792 (93.3%) — POLY 285/294, Ldr 25/33, VP4 34/36, VP2 49/49, VP3 48/48, VP1 53/57, 2A 13/16, 2B 30/41, 2C 35/35, 3A 24/28, VPG 21/27, 3C 31/36, 3D 62/62, 2A_LONG 23/24, Ldr_PRO 6/6. This is a floor, not a validation; the held-out figures are in §05 and §06.

rows: genomes ≥ 5 kb, clustered at 95% nucleotide identity

blocks.html: 25 rep contigs ship with the module; 36 of them are the best BLASTn hit for at least one exemplar. Routing was measured against the ten Picornaviridae modules only — nucleotide BLASTn cannot reach the routing threshold across virus families, and leaving the other 56 modules' 558 rep contigs out cut the run time four-fold.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: Both splits work exactly as intended, and coverage varies sharply by genus.

blocks.html: 52 of 182 routed exemplars get every one of the 11 core features. Features trailing the best-called core protein by 20 points or more: VP1, 2B, 3A. Excluded from that count: 2A, 2A_LONG, Ldr, Ldr_PRO — called by an external program and absent from this table, or a protein part of the genus does not encode.

The splits are clean. Bopivirus gets 2A_LONG on 32 of 41 and 2A on 41; Erbovirus gets Ldr_PRO on 7 of 7 and Ldr on zero; no other genus gets either. All four split features are excluded from the complete-genome count, since no genome should carry both halves of a split.

Erbovirus (7 of 7 on every feature) and Bopivirus (32–41 of 41) are covered well. Hunnivirus, the most numerous genus, is called on POLY, VP4, VP2, VP3, 2A, 2C, 3C and 3D but on zero of 76 for VP1, 2B, 3A and the leader. Anativirus misses VP1 and 3A; Tottorivirus misses VP1, 2A, 2B, 3A, VPg and the leader.

The panel is 39 genomes drawn round-robin across species from this genus's own BV-BRC contigs, with every rep-contig reference genome excluded, built into GTOs with rast-create-genome and scored by viral_genome_quality.pl. Genuinely clean means no genome, contig or feature flag at all.

sections.title: What it cannot do
sections.lede: Four features are missing from the most numerous genus, and the training data says why.

blocks.html: Hunnivirus has 122 polyprotein sequences and almost no annotated mature peptides. It contributes 0 sequences to VP1, and 2 each to 2B, 3A and the leader — against 122 to POLY. It is called on VP1 zero times out of 76, and on 2B, 3A and the leader zero times.

Tottorivirus and Anativirus follow the same rule. Tottorivirus contributes 0 sequences to 3A and VP1 and gets 0 calls for both. Anativirus contributes 0 to the leader and gets 0. Where a genus contributes two or more sequences the feature is usually called; where it contributes none it never is.

This is not a threshold that can be lowered. A profile cannot be built from zero sequences, and the leftover pass — the sanctioned route to a two-member profile — has nothing to work from either. The proteins are present in these genomes; the polyprotein is called on 122 Hunnivirus records. What is missing is any annotated example of the mature peptide to train on.

The fix that would work is projection, and it was not applied here. Three genus modules in this family had the same shape — many polyproteins, few annotated mature peptides — and were rebuilt by carrying cut coordinates from the annotated genomes onto the rest across a global alignment. That technique took the Sapelovirus leader from 6 calls in 209 to 170 in 208. It was not run on the grouped modules, and Hunnivirus with 122 polyproteins and 0 annotated VP1 records is exactly the case it is designed for.

Both genus-conditional splits work and neither feature ever fires on the wrong genus. Erbovirus and Bopivirus are well covered; Hunnivirus misses four features because it contributes zero or two sequences to each of them while contributing 122 polyproteins. That last fact makes this module the strongest candidate in the family for a projection rebuild, which has not been done.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: The run located a fix that exists and was not applied.

blocks.html: The splits were decided before building, by comparing per-genus medians inside each slot, and the coverage run confirms both were right: each form is called on its own genera and never on the others.

What the run also shows is that the grouped modules were built without the projection step that was applied to Avihepatovirus, Hepatovirus, Kobuvirus, Senecavirus and Sapelovirus. Those five had the same problem — polyproteins in abundance, annotated mature peptides scarce — and projection roughly tripled their collections. Hunnivirus here has 122 polyproteins and zero annotated VP1 records, which is the clearest instance of that shape anywhere in the family. Applying it is the obvious next work on this module and is recorded as such rather than presented as done.

Rarefaction over proteins: every annotated protein in the 191 genomes both sources annotate (683 source product records, 2,001 module calls) shuffled 100 times and drawn one at a time. Both curves start at zero. The source vocabulary reaches 56 distinct strings, the module's 18. At the depth both reach, 683 proteins, free text has used 56.0 strings against 16.4 — a 3.4-fold difference. The source reaches 95% of its final size after 636 proteins, the module after 1,117.
